question: We made a tool that only takes the grades teachers already gave and calculates the weighted average. Is this still a high-risk AI system?
gold_source: Article 6(3), first subparagraph, point (a); Article 6(3), last subparagraph; Article 6(2)
gold_answer: Not necessarily. Annex III systems are high-risk (Article 6(2)), but under Article 6(3)(a) a system that only performs a narrow procedural task is not considered high-risk if it does not pose a significant risk of harm. This exception never applies if the system performs profiling of natural persons (Article 6(3), last subparagraph).

question: Our AI reads the exam a teacher prepared and points out mistakes, like typos or unclear questions. It does not change the questions or make them easier or harder. Is this a problem under the AI Act?
gold_answer: Article 6(3)(b) says an Annex III system is not considered high-risk when it is intended to improve the result of a previously completed human activity and does not pose a significant risk of harm; checking an exam the teacher already wrote fits this description. A provider relying on this must document its assessment before release (Article 6(4)), and the exception does not apply if the system profiles natural persons.

question: Okay, and if we decide our grade calculator is not high-risk, do we still have to do anything before we launch it?
gold_answer: Yes. Under Article 6(4) the provider must document its assessment before the system is placed on the market or put into service, and must give it to national competent authorities on request. Under Article 49(2) the provider must also register itself and the system in the EU database before release.

question: We want to add a webcam feature that notices when students look bored or frustrated, so the lesson can change. Are we allowed to do this?
gold_answer: Article 5(1)(f) prohibits placing on the market, putting into service or using AI systems that infer the emotions of a natural person in education institutions. The only exception is when the system is intended for medical or safety reasons; adapting a lesson is neither.

question: If our grading system counts as high-risk, what rules does it have to follow?
gold_answer: Article 8 says high-risk systems must meet the requirements of Articles 9 to 15: a risk management system (Article 9), quality training, validation and test data (Article 10), technical documentation drawn up before release (Article 11), automatic logging (Article 12), transparency and instructions for the deployer (Article 13), human oversight (Article 14), and an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity (Article 15).
